newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, with spreads to U.S. Treasuries narrowing ahead of key public testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

"With the uncertainty in the U.S. market, should the U.S. deteriorate, Canada should outperform. I think we're seeing that trade again," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed income with Altamira Investment Services.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.40 to C$107.85 to yield 7.322 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.91.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 41 basis points from 42 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canadian bonds closed stronger in a session which saw volatile U.S. trading linked to the first U.S. auction of 10-year, inflation-indexed bonds. U.S. volatility was also linked to apprehension that Greenspan's testimony tomorrow will prompt a wide swing in prices.

While Canada had no new government supply today, analysts said the market also benefitted from buying related to the approaching deadline for investors to place money in registered retirement savings plans.

"I think what's also helping the situation, helping Canada outperform, is we're entering this time of year where you get a lot of flows coming into capital markets with RRSPs," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.35 to C$102.40 to yield 6.661 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to three basis points from seven basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.89 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.18 percent.
